agent: startsave (OpenHOI3 worktree agent): the start save against a new game
question: What sets a country's shares of IC at the start; when a new game's Lua changes of law take effect against its two first days; which of a minister's two types for one post is his

addresses.name: Enter_SetNewGameShares
addresses.comment: **Where a new game's six shares of IC are set**: in CInGameIdler::Enter's new-game block, per country, straight after SetUpCountryForNewGame (0x65B4F2) and CCountry::RecountUnitTotals (0x65B4F7, which counts land_brigades_in_service +0x108C). `call CCountry::GetConsumerGoodsNeeded` (this in EAX, thousandths out through ESI = [esp+0xBC]); cg = (demand << 30) / 0x1F40000 - the thousandths turned into a 48.15 share, truncated (0x65B50A-0x65B52E); rest = ((0x8000 - cg) << 15) / 0x28000 - a fifth of what is left, truncated (0x65B535-0x65B55A). Then for i in 0..5 the share object ProductionDistribution (+0x5F4)[i] gets base_percentage (+8/+0xC) = rest, its slot 4 called where the value changed (0x65B580-0x65B5D8); then [1], consumer goods, gets cg the same way (0x65B5DA-0x65B620). So the demand is the one of that moment: under the laws SetUpCountryLawsAndTechnologyForNewGame brought forward (the Lua's Laws() posts are still on the queue), with the standing-army term over the units just read, and without the ministers the set-up's filling of empty posts gives. Measured: the 24 untouched countries of the start save (the 23 that do not exist and Germany) all agree, Germany 0.22400 = 0.200 + 0.024 for 33 brigades on 201 IC at neutrality 60. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-startshares.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x65B4D4-0x65B622 (scripts/disasm.py): the call to 0x4FA020 at 0x65B505 is one of its four callers (findRefs --callers 0x4FA020: 0x518FBA, 0x519044, 0x51926F, 0x65B505); the two __alldiv calls at 0x65B529 (divisor 0x1F40000) and 0x65B55A (divisor 0x28000); the loop's bound `cmp eax, 0x18` over 4-byte slots of [esi+0x5F4]; the stores to [ecx+8]/[ecx+0xC]. Wrong if [esi+0x5F4] were not the six IC shares - it is the vector RunCountryDailyPass walks for the six (FINDINGS-distribute.md section 1).

addresses.name: SetUpCountryForNewGame_CallLaws
addresses.comment: **The new game's call of the Lua global `Laws(country)`** (GetThreadLuaState, PrepareLuaCall_Laws 0x510120, LuaCallProxy_Country_CallVoid 0x50D3F0, to 0x4D7375), after ReapplyAllTechnologies and before RebuildStaticModifiers, UpdateMaxManpower and `manpower = max_manpower`. **What it posts waits on the session's queue and is run after the new game's two first days**: CCurrentGameState.Post sends the command's copy through in_game_screen slot 18 to the queue at +0x38 slot 6, the queue that also carries CHourlyTickCommand and that the session drains outside CInGameIdler::Enter, asking IsValid again before Execute (FINDINGS-tick.md; CChangeLawCommand::IsValid's comment); Enter itself runs the two days at 0x65CB2E/0x65CC64, later in the same call. So the days run under the laws the engine's own pass gave, the manpower pool is the most under those laws, and the change of law is made afterwards - its tail holding every brigade to the running game's ceilings and pricing the build queue again. Inferred for the drain's place (likely: not traced to its loop); measured on the start save: 16 untouched countries' supplies fit only the industrial policy before the change, 74 countries' brigades are held to the running ceilings, and Germany's manpower 882 is the two-year draft's, the engine pass's law. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-startshares.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x4D7346-0x4D737C: ReapplyAllTechnologies (0x532840), GetThreadLuaState (0x8EACA0), PrepareLuaCall_Laws (0x510120), LuaCallProxy_Country_CallVoid (0x50D3F0). The queue route is the record's CCurrentGameState.Post (rva 0x4E9BB0) and the tick posted through the same slot (FINDINGS-tick.md, The clock). Built so in OpenHOI3 on 2026-11-14, a new game is the start save's in every brigade's organisation (3,792 of 3,792, from 962), every country's dissent and national unity, and 100 of 101 alignments. Wrong if the queue's post executed synchronously when in_game is clear - the save's held brigades and supplies would then not fit; a live breakpoint on CChangeLawCommand::Execute (0x54EF60) during a new game, read against the tick counter and whether RunDailyPass has run, settles it.

addresses.name: CMinister_LoadKey_AppendPosting
addresses.comment: **A posting is appended at the tail of the minister's list**: the new 0x14-byte node {position, type, prev = old tail (+0x60), next 0, byte 0} becomes the tail (`mov [edx+0x60], eax`), the count (+0x64) goes up, and the old tail's next (+0xC) is linked to it - or, the list being empty, the head (+0x5C) is (0x52C86C). CMinister::GetPersonality (0x52CBE0) walks from the head and answers the first posting whose position matches. **So the first type a `ministers` block gives for a post is the minister's, and a second line for the same post is never seen.** Measured: Honduras's armament minister 79004 is declared laissez_faires_capitalist and then resource_industrialist; the start save's energy for Honduras, 17.500, is 7.5 under basic_mobilisation's -25% without the second's +5% global_resources (the second would give 18.000). The base game gives a post twice or more 270 times, 71 with different types. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-startshares.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x52C80F-0x52C86F (the node fill at 0x52C828-0x52C833, the tail and count stores at 0x52C844/0x52C847, the old tail's link at 0x52C852, the head store at 0x52C86C) and 0x52CBE0-0x52CC64 (GetPersonality: `mov ecx,[ecx+0x5c]`, then `cmp edx, esi; je` before following +0xC). Wrong if the country modifier's rebuild found a minister's type by another walk than the first match - the Honduras figure says it does not take the last, and a both-applied reading would give 18.000 as well.
